考試官教授譚批：〔辭理明當。〕
考試官教授劉批：〔得謹嚴體。〕

《春秋》重君臣之義，故兩予霸兵以致意焉。此宋之圍、鄭之伐，皆關於君臣之大義也，《春秋》寧不深與之乎？昔晉悼嗣霸，以魚石叛宋而楚、鄭助之也，於是討魚石，圍彭城，遂伐鄭而次鄫焉。君子曰：美哉晉師！其皆放義而行者乎！何則？不登
translation_en:
… cautious! Moreover, at that time a hegemon such as Duke Huan of Qi (齊桓) also once harbored ambitions of encroaching upon Lu. Had it not been for Jizi (季子), how could Lu have dispelled both internal and external crises and placed the state in security? The Book of Documents (Shu 書) says: "The glory and tranquility of a state also depend upon the felicity of one man." From this I know how beneficial worthy talents are to a state.

"Zhongsun Mie (仲孫蔑) met with Luan Yan (欒黶) of Jin, Hua Yuan (華元) of Song, Ning Zhi (甯殖) of Wei, and men of Cao, Ju, Zhu, Teng, and Xue to lay siege to Pengcheng (彭城) in Song. In summer, Han Jue (韓厥) of Jin led an army to attack Zheng, and Zhongsun Mie met with Cui Zhu (崔杼) of Qi and men of Cao, Zhu, and Qi, halting at Zeng (鄫)." [Both from the first year of Duke Xiang (襄公).]
By Zhou Danian (周大年).
Comment by Associate Examiner Subprefectural Instructor Jiang (姜): [This piece deeply accords with the meaning of the commentary; moreover, its diction is strict and its style rectified—it can] serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner Prefectural Instructor Tan (譚): [The diction and reasoning are clear and fitting.]
Comment by Examiner Prefectural Instructor Liu (劉): [It attains a scrupulous and rigorous style.]

The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) attaches great weight to the moral duty between ruler and minister, and thus twice approves the hegemon's military expeditions in order to convey this principle. Both this siege in Song and the attack on Zheng concerned the great moral duty between ruler and minister; how could the Spring and Autumn Annals not deeply approve of them? Formerly, when Duke Dao of Jin (晉悼) succeeded to the hegemony, because Yu Shi (魚石) rebelled against Song and Chu and Zheng aided him, Duke Dao therefore punished Yu Shi, laid siege to Pengcheng, and thereupon attacked Zheng and halted at Zeng. The gentleman says: How admirable were the armies of Jin! Were they not all acting in accordance with righteousness? Why is this so? Not elevating …

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
叛人天下大義也楚雖變夷之國獨不知君臣
之分乎顧乃肆意魚石之封畀以彭城之入則
宋之大分自楚紊矣幸而晉也當虛朾既盟之
後舉誅亂討賊之師環邑示罰降城歸地以五
大夫還而置諸瓠丘焉卒使魚石叛君之罪無
所容楚人黨叛之謀無所濟大分既紊而復正
此一圍之功也春秋于圍彭城而必係以宋者
若曰楚不得取之宋魚石不得受之楚與晉之
義見矣若擇義而從小國令圖也鄭雖附夷之
===
國獨不明君臣之義乎顧乃甘心從楚之私連
兵魚石之黨則宋之大義自鄭亂矣幸而晉也
當彭城既圍之後爲聲罪致討之師入鄭示懲
敗洧示威合諸侯之師而次于鄫地焉卒使鄭
人朋姦之罪無所逃楚人救鄭之兵無所用大
義既亂而復明此一伐之功也春秋于伐鄭而
不書楚救者若曰鄭無可救之善楚不得有能
救之名與晉之義益見矣此義行則誅討之法
嚴而背叛之禍熄春秋經世之慮其深乎抑于
punctuated: 叛人，天下大義也。楚雖變夷之國，獨不知君臣之分乎？顧乃肆意魚石之封，畀以彭城之入，則宋之大分自楚紊矣。幸而晉也，當虛朾既盟之後，舉誅亂討賊之師，環邑示罰，降城歸地，以五大夫還，而置諸瓠丘焉。卒使魚石叛君之罪無所容，楚人黨叛之謀無所濟，大分既紊而復正，此一圍之功也。《春秋》于圍彭城而必係以宋者，若曰：楚不得取之宋，魚石不得受之楚，與晉之義見矣。若擇義而從，小國令圖也。鄭雖附夷之國，獨不明君臣之義乎？顧乃甘心從楚之私，連兵魚石之黨，則宋之大義自鄭亂矣。幸而晉也，當彭城既圍之後，爲聲罪致討之師，入鄭示懲，敗洧示威，合諸侯之師而次于鄫地焉。卒使鄭人朋姦之罪無所逃，楚人救鄭之兵無所用，大義既亂而復明，此一伐之功也。《春秋》于伐鄭而不書楚救者，若曰：鄭無可救之善，楚不得有能救之名，與晉之義益見矣。此義行，則誅討之法嚴而背叛之禍熄，《春秋》經世之慮其深乎！抑于
translation_en:
… rebels is a great principle of righteousness under heaven. Even though Chu was a state that had degenerated into barbarian ways, how could it alone be ignorant of the proper distinction between ruler and minister? Yet it willfully enfeoffed Yu Shi 魚石 and granted him the revenues of Pengcheng 彭城; thus the great distinction in Song 宋 was thrown into disorder by Chu. Fortunately, after the covenant at Xudeng 虛朾, Jin 晉 raised an army to punish disorder and chastise traitors. Surrounding the town to display punishment, it forced the city to surrender, returned the territory to Song, brought back the five grandees, and confined them at Huqiu 瓠丘. In the end, Yu Shi's crime of rebelling against his ruler had nowhere to be tolerated, and the people of Chu's plot to side with rebels came to naught. The great distinction, once thrown into disorder, was rectified again—such was the achievement of this single siege. That the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), in recording the siege of Pengcheng, insisted on tying it to Song is as if to say: Chu had no right to seize it from Song, and Yu Shi had no right to receive it from Chu; thus its approval of Jin's righteousness is made manifest.

As for choosing righteousness and following it, that is the proper plan for a small state. Even though Zheng 鄭 was a state that attached itself to barbarians, how could it alone be unclear about the righteousness between ruler and minister? Yet it willingly followed the selfish interests of Chu and joined arms with the faction of Yu Shi; thus the great righteousness in Song was thrown into confusion by Zheng. Fortunately, after Pengcheng had been besieged, Jin raised an army to denounce the crime and exact punishment. Entering Zheng to display chastisement and defeating them at the Wei 洧 River to display majesty, it united the armies of the feudal lords and encamped in the territory of Zeng 鄫. In the end, the people of Zheng's crime of colluding with the wicked had no way of escape, and the troops of Chu sent to rescue Zheng were rendered useless. The great righteousness, once thrown into confusion, was made clear again—such was the achievement of this single punitive expedition. That the Spring and Autumn Annals, in recording the expedition against Zheng, did not record Chu's rescue is as if to say: Zheng had no goodness worthy of being rescued, and Chu could not be allowed the reputation of being able to rescue; thus its approval of Jin's righteousness is made even more manifest. When this righteousness is put into practice, the laws of punishment and chastisement become strict and the calamities of rebellion are extinguished. How profound is the Spring and Autumn Annals' concern for ordering the world! Moreover, from…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
是而知晉悼復霸之易也嗣位之初他務未遑
而能首倡大義於天下宜諸侯景從而能繼桓
文霸業之盛也悼有君子之資於圍宋伐鄭而
益信其然矣噫此其所以能霸
禮記
作者之謂聖
同考試官教諭張　批〔禮樂之情根天地人心說聖人即德合天地首出人類者是作得之〕
陳遇文
===
考試官教授譚　批〔發揮精切〕
考試官教授劉　批〔醇雅〕
建禮樂之極聖人之能事也蓋禮樂必待人而
興也然則先天下而建其極者不謂之聖而何
且禮樂之道有情以立其本有文以彰其用知
其情而作之者難矣夫曰作則軌範自我昭而
創建於一心有以垂百王之懿憲法制自我定
而經始於一時有以立萬世之典章其大禮同
節者知此合敬之情而協義以起之也其大樂
punctuated:
是而知晉悼復霸之易也。嗣位之初，他務未遑，而能首倡大義於天下，宜諸侯景從，而能繼桓、文霸業之盛也。悼有君子之資，於圍宋、伐鄭而益信其然矣。噫！此其所以能霸。

《禮記》
「作者之謂聖」
同考試官教諭張　批〔禮樂之情根天地人心說，聖人即德合天地、首出人類者是。作得之。〕

建禮樂之極，聖人之能事也。蓋禮樂必待人而興也，然則先天下而建其極者，不謂之聖而何？且禮樂之道，有情以立其本，有文以彰其用；知其情而作之者，難矣。夫曰「作」，則軌範自我昭，而創建於一心，有以垂百王之懿憲；法制自我定，而經始於一時，有以立萬世之典章。其大禮同節者，知此合敬之情，而協義以起之也；其大樂
translation_en:
… this we know how easy it was for Duke Dao of Jin (Jin Dao 晉悼) to restore the hegemony. At the very beginning of his succession to the throne, before he had leisure to attend to other affairs, he was able first to champion great righteousness throughout the realm. It was fitting that the feudal lords followed him like shadows, and that he was able to continue the flourishing hegemonic achievements of Dukes Huan and Wen. That Duke Dao possessed the qualities of a gentleman is all the more credibly demonstrated in the siege of Song (at Pengcheng) and the punitive expedition against Zheng. Alas! This is why he was able to achieve hegemony.

Record of Rites (Liji 禮記)
"He who creates is called a sage."
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhang 張 comments: [Explaining that the essential reality of rites and music is rooted in Heaven, Earth, and the human mind, and that the sage is none other than one whose virtue matches Heaven and Earth and who stands foremost above humanity—this captures it in composition.]
By Chen Yuwen 陳遇文
Examiner, Instructor Tan 譚 comments: [The elaboration is incisive and apt.]
Examiner, Instructor Liu 劉 comments: [Pure and elegant.]

To establish the supreme standard of rites and music is the accomplishment proper to a sage. Indeed, rites and music must await the right person in order to arise; if so, then what else could one who precedes the world in establishing their supreme standard be called if not a sage? Moreover, in the Way of rites and music, there is inner reality (qing) by which to establish their root, and outward pattern (wen) by which to manifest their function; to comprehend their inner reality and create them is difficult indeed. Now, when we speak of "creating," it means that the models and norms are illuminated from within oneself, and being founded through the single mind, are able to hand down admirable statutes for a hundred kings; the laws and institutions are settled from within oneself, and being initiated in a single era, are able to establish canonical standards for ten thousand generations. title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
同和者知此合愛之情而因心以出之也是非
聖人能之乎心思通乎性命而無體之中有全
禮斯節之爲有體之文此之謂聖人履中正也
至德協於天人而無聲之中有至樂斯制之爲
有聲之用此之謂聖人樂和平也先天以開人
其聰明之天縱者乎而明作禮樂蓋幽贊神明
者爲之也緣情以作則其睿知之性生者乎而
極建中和蓋德合天地者能事也謂非聖人而
何信乎禮樂爲經世之大典聖人爲命世之至
===
人所謂待人而興者與故曰不聞性與天道而
能制禮作樂者未也雖然作者固謂聖矣聖如
夫子乃述而不作何耶蓋德者本也時者會也
位者權也必三重備而後禮樂可以作矣故周
公操時位以定經制成周禮樂郁郁定百代章
程焉夫子有聖人之德而時則春秋分則素王
是以徒見周公於夢寐寄禮樂於刪定焉耳然
則有位與時者其於禮樂之道宜何如
其舜禹文王周公之謂與有君民之大德
punctuated:
同和者，知此合愛之情，而因心以出之也。是非聖人能之乎？心思通乎性命，而無體之中有全禮，斯節之爲有體之文，此之謂聖人履中正也；至德協於天人，而無聲之中有至樂，斯制之爲有聲之用，此之謂聖人樂和平也。先天以開人，其聰明之天縱者乎？而明作禮樂，蓋幽贊神明者爲之也；緣情以作則，其睿知之性生者乎？而極建中和，蓋德合天地者能事也。謂非聖人而何？信乎禮樂爲經世之大典，聖人爲命世之至人，所謂待人而興者與！故曰：「不聞性與天道，而能制禮作樂者，未也。」雖然，作者固謂聖矣，聖如夫子，乃述而不作，何耶？蓋德者，本也；時者，會也；位者，權也。必三重備，而後禮樂可以作矣。故周公操時位以定經制，成周禮樂郁郁，定百代章程焉；夫子有聖人之德，而時則春秋，分則素王，是以徒見周公於夢寐，寄禮樂於刪定焉耳。然則有位與時者，其於禮樂之道，宜何如？

其舜、禹、文王、周公之謂與！有君民之大德，
translation_en:
… share the same harmony, it is because one understands this feeling of uniting in love and brings it forth from the mind. Could anyone other than a sage be capable of this? When the thoughts of the mind penetrate human nature and destiny, and within that which has no physical form there exists complete ritual, one then regulates it into tangible patterns—this is what is meant by the sage treading in centrality and correctness. When supreme virtue harmonizes with Heaven and man, and within that which has no sound there exists supreme music, one then fashions it into audible function—this is what is meant by the sage delighting in harmony and peace. Preceding Heaven to enlighten mankind—is he not one whose intelligence is Heaven-bestowed? And visibly creating rites and music is done by one who mysteriously assists the spiritual and bright. Following human feelings to establish standards—is he not one whose perspicacity and wisdom are innate? And establishing the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony is the achievement of one whose virtue matches Heaven and Earth. If we do not call him a sage, then what is he? Truly, rites and music are the great canons for ordering the world, and the sage is the supreme man ordained for the age—is this not what is meant by waiting for the right person to flourish? Therefore it is said: "Without hearing of human nature and the Way of Heaven, no one has ever been able to institute rites and create music." Even so, a creator is assuredly called a sage; yet why did a sage like the Master [Confucius] transmit without creating? It is because virtue is the foundation, timeliness is the opportunity, and position is the authority. Only when these three weighty essentials are complete can rites and music be created. Thus the Duke of Zhou held both the timely opportunity and the position to establish the constant institutions, so that the rites and music of the Zhou at its height were resplendent, fixing the statutes for a hundred generations. The Master possessed the virtue of a sage, yet his time was the Spring and Autumn period and his lot was that of an uncrowned king; therefore he could merely see the Duke of Zhou in his dreams and entrust rites and music to his editing and fixing of the texts. This being so, for one who possesses both position and the timely opportunity, how ought he to act with regard to the Way of rites and music?

"Does this not refer to Shun, Yu, King Wen, and the Duke of Zhou! Having the great virtue to rule the people, …"

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
有事君之小心
同考試官教諭張　批〔本旨重在事君小心上作者類〕閻國魁
〔不知此子能抑揚發明經學之邃者也可式〕
考試官教授譚　批〔認題明白〕
考試官教授劉　批〔典雅〕
聖人贊羣聖盡臣道以其厚於仁也夫臣道莫
難於盡仁也德大而心小焉羣聖之所以立臣
極乎夫子之言蓋曰人臣貴於有德而尤貴於
===
忘其德忘其德而純心以事君者厚於仁者也
詩以求福不回歸諸凱弟君子者何謂與蓋德
有未盛不能嚴欽翼之誠心有未純難以盡篤
棐之節其惟舜禹之守臣道於唐虞乎文王周
公之共臣職於殷周乎則求福不回之謂矣何
以言之人臣庇民以德而事君以心有大德者
未必其有小心也惟此羣聖容保之度所以宏
庇乎生民而宜君宜王者既有此大德也精白
之忱所以祇承於厥辟而有嚴有翼者又有此
punctuated:
有事君之小心。」
同考試官教諭張批〔本旨重在事君小心上，作者類〕閻國魁〔不知此。子能抑揚發明，經學之邃者也，可式。〕
考試官教授譚批〔認題明白。〕
考試官教授劉批〔典雅。〕
聖人贊羣聖盡臣道，以其厚於仁也。夫臣道莫難於盡仁也，德大而心小焉，羣聖之所以立臣極乎！夫子之言蓋曰：人臣貴於有德，而尤貴於忘其德。忘其德而純心以事君者，厚於仁者也。《詩》以「求福不回」歸諸「凱弟君子」者，何謂與？蓋德有未盛，不能嚴欽翼之誠；心有未純，難以盡篤棐之節。其惟舜、禹之守臣道於唐、虞乎？文王、周公之共臣職於殷、周乎？則「求福不回」之謂矣。何以言之？人臣庇民以德，而事君以心，有大德者未必其有小心也。惟此羣聖，容保之度所以宏庇乎生民，而宜君宜王者，既有此大德也；精白之忱所以祇承於厥辟，而有嚴有翼者，又有此
translation_en:
… and have the circumspect mind required to serve their ruler."

Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang comments: [The main purport of the passage places its emphasis on having a circumspect mind in serving the ruler; writers generally] Yan Guokui 閻國魁 [fail to realize this. This candidate is able to modulate his tone and elucidate the meaning—one whose classical learning is profound. Worthy of serving as a model.]
Examiner and Professor Tan comments: [Grasps the theme clearly.]
Examiner and Professor Liu comments: [Classically elegant.]

The Sage praised the several sages for fulfilling the way of a minister because of the abundance of their humanity. Now, in the way of a minister, nothing is more difficult than fulfilling humanity. Great in virtue yet circumspect in mind—is this not whereby the several sages established the ultimate standard for ministers?

The Master's words mean to say: For a minister, it is precious to possess virtue, yet even more precious to forget his own virtue. One who forgets his virtue and serves his ruler with a pure mind is abundant in humanity. When the Book of Odes (Shi) attributes "seeking blessings without swerving" to the "joyous and brotherly gentleman," what does it mean? For if one's virtue is not yet flourishing, one cannot maintain the sincerity of reverent respect; if one's mind is not yet pure, it is difficult to fulfill the integrity of steadfast assistance. Was this not uniquely exemplified by Shun and Yu upholding the way of the minister in the eras of Tang and Yu? And by King Wen and the Duke of Zhou discharging the duties of a minister in the Yin and Zhou dynasties? This is what is meant by "seeking blessings without swerving."

How may this be explained? A minister shelters the people through his virtue and serves his ruler through his mind; yet one who possesses great virtue does not necessarily possess a circumspect mind. Only with these several sages was their capacity to tolerate and protect—whereby they broadly sheltered the living people and were fit to be lords and fit to be kings—already such great virtue; and their pure, unblemished devotion—whereby they reverently attended upon their sovereign, solemn and respectful—was moreover this…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
小心焉曰好生曰惠迪舜禹之德固足以秉天
下矣然德愈盛而心愈虛惟兢兢焉知臣道之
當守而已他何知焉爲惠鮮爲師保文王周公
之德固可以毗斯世矣然德愈隆而心愈下惟
翼翼焉知臣職之當共而已他何計焉德優於
庇民而心純於報主仁之厚也孰加焉信乎其
求福不回也欲爲臣盡臣道者法四聖而已矣
抑四聖大德小心夫子知之天下萬世法之四
聖人不知也蓋中心安仁而師師蹇蹇者一無
所爲而爲也此讓德祇承事殷復辟恪共弗易
也一有利之之心則回矣回豈臣之福哉宋臣
曰爲之自我者當如是其知純臣之心者歟
第貳場
論
人主當務聰明之實
司馬晰
同考試官教諭李　批
立意純正氣格雄渾無一塵套
論之翹楚也
punctuated:
小心焉。曰「好生」、曰「惠迪」，舜、禹之德固足以秉天下矣；然德愈盛而心愈虛，惟兢兢焉知臣道之當守而已，他何知焉？爲「惠鮮」、爲「師保」，文王、周公之德固可以毗斯世矣；然德愈隆而心愈下，惟翼翼焉知臣職之當共而已，他何計焉？德優於庇民，而心純於報主，仁之厚也，孰加焉？信乎其「求福不回」也！欲爲臣盡臣道者，法四聖而已矣。抑四聖大德小心，夫子知之，天下萬世法之，四聖人不知也。蓋中心安仁，而師師、蹇蹇者，一無所爲而爲也。此讓德、祇承、事殷、復辟，恪共弗易也。一有利之之心，則回矣，回豈臣之福哉？宋臣曰：「爲之自我者當如是。」其知純臣之心者歟！

第貳場
論
《人主當務聰明之實》
司馬晰
同考試官教諭李　批：立意純正，氣格雄渾，無一塵套，論之翹楚也。
translation_en:
… prudently circumspect mind. Described as "loving life" and "following the right path," the virtue of Shun and Yu was certainly sufficient to hold sway over the world; yet the more flourishing their virtue, the more humble their minds, cautiously knowing only that the way of a minister ought to be upheld—what else did they know? Acting with "kindness to the destitute" and serving as "Grand Tutor and Grand Guardian," the virtue of King Wen and the Duke of Zhou was certainly able to assist the age; yet the more exalted their virtue, the more modest their minds, reverently knowing only that the duties of a minister ought to be fulfilled—what else did they calculate? When virtue is abundant in sheltering the people and the mind is pure in repaying the ruler, such is the thickness of benevolence—what could surpass it? Truly, this is what is meant by "seeking blessings without deviance"! Those who wish to act as ministers and exhaust the way of a minister need only model themselves on these four sages.

Moreover, that the four sages possessed great virtue and yet maintained a prudently circumspect mind was understood by the Master and taken as a model by all under heaven for ten thousand generations, though the four sages themselves were unconscious of it. For they rested peacefully in benevolence within their hearts, and their mutual emulation and loyal candor were practiced without any ulterior motive whatsoever. Thus, in yielding because of virtue, reverently receiving commands, serving Yin, and restoring the throne to the sovereign, they remained reverently diligent and unchanging. The moment there is a mind set on personal advantage, it becomes deviant—and how could deviance be a blessing for a minister? A minister of the Song dynasty said: "What it rests with me to do ought to be done like this." Did he not understand the heart of a pure minister!

Second Session
Discourse
"A Ruler Ought to Strive for the Reality of Perceptiveness and Understanding" (Renzhu dang wu congming zhi shi)
Sima Xi 司馬晰
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li: The conception of the theme is pure and upright, the spirit and style are vigorous and grand, without a single hackneyed cliché; it is an outstanding piece among the discourses.

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授譚　批〔章法句法棹有古意〕
考試官教授劉　批〔古雅雄健〕
人主以至公之心治天下而不役其身以爲天
下用何者人主不能以獨治天下舉天下之事
而付之於臣臣者佐主以圖治而凡主之智之
不及謀力之不及爲者彼皆盡心以謀之爲之
而卒歸功於其主故明主以至公之心求天下
之賢寄之以腹心股肱之任然後聰明之用益
廣而天下之治日益精明而不可及苟恃一己
===
之聰明總總焉役其身以求治而天下之事紛
至沓來遺於耳目之外者卒無以濟而聰明之
用亦窮此名實之辨勞逸之分治忽之機不可
不察也今夫天之道公而已矣以聰明寄之民
而無容心書曰天聰明自我民聰明知天則知
君矣夫天之生君豈其使一人巍然寄於民上
而無所作用哉當必有聰明睿知首出庶物之
資以爲用人行政之本故曰亶聰明作元后蓋
厚之也夫惟受之者異也人主不得不以聰明
punctuated:
考試官教授譚批〔章法句法，棹有古意。〕
考試官教授劉批〔古雅雄健。〕

人主以至公之心治天下，而不役其身以爲天下用。何者？人主不能以獨治天下，舉天下之事而付之於臣。臣者，佐主以圖治，而凡主之智之不及謀、力之不及爲者，彼皆盡心以謀之、爲之，而卒歸功於其主。故明主以至公之心求天下之賢，寄之以腹心股肱之任，然後聰明之用益廣，而天下之治日益精明而不可及。苟恃一己之聰明，總總焉役其身以求治，而天下之事紛至沓來，遺於耳目之外者卒無以濟，而聰明之用亦窮。此名實之辨、勞逸之分、治忽之機，不可不察也。

今夫天之道，公而已矣，以聰明寄之民而無容心。《書》曰：「天聰明，自我民聰明。」知天則知君矣。夫天之生君，豈其使一人巍然寄於民上而無所作用哉？當必有聰明睿知、首出庶物之資，以爲用人行政之本。故曰：「亶聰明，作元后。」蓋厚之也。夫惟受之者異也，人主不得不以聰明…
translation_en:
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Tan comments: [Its compositional and sentence structures are vigorous [?] with an antique spirit.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu comments: [Classically elegant and forcefully vigorous.]

A ruler governs the realm with a mind of utmost impartiality, and does not enslave his own person in service to the realm. Why is this? A ruler cannot govern the realm alone, so he takes all the affairs of the realm and entrusts them to his ministers. Ministers are those who assist the ruler in planning for good governance; in all matters where the ruler's wisdom falls short of planning or his strength falls short of acting, they exhaust their minds to plan them and carry them out, and in the end attribute the merit to their ruler. Therefore, an enlightened ruler seeks out the worthy men of the realm with a mind of utmost impartiality and entrusts them with the responsibilities of heart and limbs. Only then does the reach of his perspicacity and acuity grow ever broader, and the governance of the realm becomes daily more refined, clear, and unattainable by others. If, instead, he relies upon his own personal perspicacity and acuity, busily enslaving his own person in pursuit of order, then as the affairs of the realm come crowding in from all sides, those that escape his own ears and eyes will in the end have no means of being resolved, and the functioning of his perspicacity and acuity will likewise be exhausted. Herein lie the distinction between name and reality, the division between toil and ease, and the pivot between order and neglect—they cannot but be examined.

Now, the Way of Heaven is nothing other than impartiality; it entrusts its perspicacity and acuity to the people and harbors no private calculation of its own. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Heaven hears and sees as our people hear and see." If one understands Heaven, one understands the ruler. When Heaven gives birth to a ruler, how could it merely set one man loftily above the people with nothing to do? He must surely possess the endowments of perspicacity, acuity, and sagely wisdom that rise preeminent above the multitude of things, to serve as the foundation for employing men and conducting government. Therefore it is said: "Truly perspicacious and acute, he becomes the great sovereign." This is because Heaven has endowed him generously. Now, precisely because what he has received is extraordinary, the ruler cannot help but use his perspicacity and acuity…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
爲天下用用然託之者重且大也人主又不敢不
以用聰明爲天下愼故務實則公公則逸務名
則私私則勞而治忽因之然則人主之用聰明
亦在乎知務而已矣昔者稱人主之聰明有曰
雄才大略也綜核名實也强明自任也之數者
世之所矜快炫誇而明主不務也何者彼騖於
名而鮮實也故以才略名者耗海內以綜核書
者索元氣而伺人隱伏旁窺苛察者無裨於藩
鎮之跋扈則是務名之過而寡實之效也是故
===
前鄭後衞易惑也左許右史易蔽也一暴十寒
易息也故一堵之外目有所不見一室之間耳
有所不聞以壅蔽蠱惑者衆也甚矣人主之無
樂於務名而役其身以爲天下用也故務實莫
若公公者何所謂純心任賢相與圖天下之治
者也今夫泰山高矣而土壤附焉河海深矣而
細流歸焉何者卑者高之基大者小之積也人
主之用聰明亦若是而已夫世未有有君而無
臣者也而人品不同孟軻氏所稱安社稷以上
punctuated: 爲天下用用，然託之者重且大也，人主又不敢不以用聰明爲天下愼。故務實則公，公則逸；務名則私，私則勞，而治忽因之。然則人主之用聰明，亦在乎知務而已矣。昔者稱人主之聰明，有曰雄才大略也，綜核名實也，强明自任也。之數者，世之所矜快炫誇，而明主不務也。何者？彼騖於名而鮮實也。故以才略名者耗海內，以綜核書者索元氣，而伺人隱伏、旁窺苛察者無裨於藩鎮之跋扈。則是務名之過，而寡實之效也。是故前鄭後衞，易惑也；左許右史，易蔽也；一暴十寒，易息也。故一堵之外，目有所不見；一室之間，耳有所不聞，以壅蔽蠱惑者衆也。甚矣，人主之無樂於務名，而役其身以爲天下用也！故務實莫若公。公者何？所謂純心任賢，相與圖天下之治者也。今夫泰山高矣，而土壤附焉；河海深矣，而細流歸焉。何者？卑者高之基，大者小之積也。人主之用聰明，亦若是而已。夫世未有有君而無臣者也，而人品不同，孟軻氏所稱安社稷以上，
translation_en: …be put to use for the world; yet because what is entrusted to him is weighty and great, the ruler also dares not fail to be cautious in exercising his intelligence and acuity for the sake of the world. Therefore, to devote oneself to reality leads to impartiality, and impartiality leads to ease; to devote oneself to reputation leads to partiality, and partiality leads to toil, and good governance or neglect follow therefrom. That being so, the ruler's exercise of intelligence and acuity lies simply in knowing what to devote himself to. In the past, those who praised the intelligence and acuity of rulers spoke of "heroic talent and grand strategy," "comprehensively verifying title and reality," and "taking personal charge with vigorous perspicacity." These several qualities are what the world takes pride in, delights in, and boasts of, yet an enlightened ruler does not pursue them. Why? Because they chase after reputation and are scant in reality. Thus, he who was famed for talent and strategy exhausted the realm within the seas; he who was recorded [?] for comprehensive verification drained the vital energy of the state; and he who spied on men's hidden secrets and engaged in sidelong prying and harsh scrutiny was of no help against the recalcitrance of the regional military commands. These are the faults of pursuing reputation and the results of lacking reality. Therefore, with the music of Zheng in front and Wei behind, it is easy to be deluded; with a Xu on the left and a Shi on the right, it is easy to be hoodwinked; with one day of warmth and ten days of cold, it is easy to slacken. Thus, beyond a single wall, there are things the eye does not see; within a single room, there are things the ear does not hear, because those who obstruct, blind, and beguile are many. Extreme indeed is the joylessness of a ruler who pursues reputation and enslaves his own person to be used by the world! Therefore, in devoting oneself to reality, nothing is better than impartiality. What is impartiality? It is what is called employing the worthy with a pure heart, working together with them to plan the governance of the world. Now, Mount Tai is high, yet clods of earth attach themselves to it; the Yellow River and the seas are deep, yet trickling streams return to them. Why? Because the low is the foundation of the high, and the great is the accumulation of the small. The ruler's exercise of intelligence and acuity is just like this and nothing more. Never in the world has there been a sovereign without ministers; yet men's characters differ, and from those whom Meng Ke (Mencius) termed "ministers who bring peace to the altars of soil and grain" on up…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
其大較可想也人主患弗用耳既用矣患弗專
耳夫惟不用不專而後人主之聰明無所寄毋
怪乎役其身以為天下用也明主知之故不以
一己之聰明為聰明而以衆人之聰明為聰明
不以臣視其臣而以一體視其臣不以上下之
分相懸隔而以一體之義相責而相成君有以
諒其臣臣亦有以諒其君日與之共論天下之
事要諸至當而督之于行故彼有所是無以其
非折之彼有所可無以其否勝之彼有所參錯
===
齟齬而相軋也無以其成要之何者至公故也
公故能虛虛則有以容天下之善公故能明明
則有以研研天下之幾由是不有其聰而聰無不
聞也不有其明而明無不見也蓋至於無無不
無不見而後天下之治猶運之掌而人君之身
其自處又甚逸假令與沾沾察察偏聽獨任者
比德較政不可同日而語矣昔在堯舜神聖濬
哲其臣有若九官十二牧而又百揆四岳總治
內外相與疇洛吁咈於一堂之上故其治雍熙
punctuated: 其大較可想也。人主患弗用耳，既用矣，患弗專耳。夫惟不用、不專，而後人主之聰明無所寄，毋怪乎役其身以為天下用也。明主知之，故不以一己之聰明為聰明，而以衆人之聰明為聰明；不以臣視其臣，而以一體視其臣；不以上下之分相懸隔，而以一體之義相責而相成。君有以諒其臣，臣亦有以諒其君，日與之共論天下之事，要諸至當，而督之于行。故彼有所是，無以其非折之；彼有所可，無以其否勝之；彼有所參錯齟齬而相軋也，無以其成要之。何者？至公故也。公故能虛，虛則有以容天下之善；公故能明，明則有以研研天下之幾。由是不有其聰，而聰無不聞也；不有其明，而明無不見也。蓋至於無無不無不見，而後天下之治猶運之掌，而人君之身其自處又甚逸。假令與沾沾察察、偏聽獨任者比德較政，不可同日而語矣。昔在堯、舜，神聖濬哲，其臣有若九官、十二牧，而又百揆、四岳總治內外，相與疇洛、吁咈於一堂之上，故其治雍熙…
translation_en: …their general distinction can be imagined. A ruler need only worry about failing to employ them; and once he employs them, he need only worry about failing to trust them exclusively. It is only when he neither employs nor trusts them exclusively that the ruler's keenness of hearing and sight has nothing on which to rely, and it is no wonder that he enslaves his own person to serve the empire. An enlightened ruler understands this. Therefore, he does not take his own personal keenness of hearing and sight as his keenness of hearing and sight, but takes the keenness of hearing and sight of the multitude as his own; he does not regard his ministers merely as ministers, but regards them as one body with himself; he does not let the distinction between superior and inferior create a gulf between them, but uses the principle of being one body to hold one another responsible and bring one another to completion. The sovereign has the means to understand and trust his ministers, and the ministers likewise have the means to understand and trust their sovereign. Every day he discusses the affairs of the empire together with them, seeking what is most appropriate and supervising its implementation. Thus, when others have something they deem right, there is no refuting it with what they get wrong; when others have something they deem acceptable, there is no overriding it with what they fail at; when others have points of divergence, friction, and mutual contention, there is no forcing the issue with preconceived conclusions [?]. Why is this? Because of utmost impartiality. Being impartial, he can be receptive; being receptive, he has the capacity to accommodate all the good in the empire. Being impartial, he can be clear-sighted; being clear-sighted, he has the capacity to thoroughly investigate [reading 研 for 研研] the subtle springs of action in the empire. Consequently, he does not claim keenness of hearing for himself, yet his hearing leaves nothing unheard; he does not claim keenness of sight for himself, yet his sight leaves nothing unseen. Indeed, when he reaches the point where nothing is unheard [reading 無不聞 for 無無不] and nothing is unseen, then governing the empire is like turning it in the palm of his hand, while the ruler himself remains in a state of great ease. Suppose one were to compare his virtue and weigh his governance against those who are petty andnitpicking, biased in listening and acting all alone—they could not be spoken of on the same day! In antiquity, Yao and Shun were divinely sage and profoundly wise. Among their ministers were the Nine Offices and Twelve Pastors, as well as the General Regulator and the Four Mountains overseeing governance within and without. Together in a single hall they inquired and consulted [reading 疇咨 for 疇洛], expressing sighs of dissent and agreement; thus their governance was harmonious, prosperous,…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
太和邈乎難及彼所謂通上下之情覈於名實
之辨而善用聰明者也故曰堯舜之知不徧物
堯舜之仁不徧愛人以親賢爲先務也抑又聞
之冕而前旒所以蔽明黈纊充耳所以塞聰若
不用聰明然者何與蓋有之而善用者人主以
飭明作之功黜之而不用者人主以養敦大之
體斯二者蓋交脩也而固人心培國脈尤在渾
厚篤實云然則人主聰明之資惟貴養之哉惟
貴養之哉此朱子未發之意也

考試官教授譚　批〔有議論有操縱〕

===
人君以天自處一憲天之外無容心矣所謂天
者非在天之天吾心之天是也夫以天下之大
舉而萃之人主之一身其不能以形爲天下役
punctuated:
太和，邈乎難及。彼所謂通上下之情，覈於名實之辨，而善用聰明者也。故曰：「堯舜之知而不徧物，堯舜之仁不徧愛人。」以親賢爲先務也。抑又聞之，冕而前旒，所以蔽明；黈纊充耳，所以塞聰。若不用聰明然者，何與？蓋有之而善用者，人主以飭明作之功；黜之而不用者，人主以養敦大之體。斯二者，蓋交脩也。而固人心、培國脈，尤在渾厚篤實云。然則人主聰明之資，惟貴養之哉！惟貴養之哉！此朱子未發之意也。

人君以天自處，一憲天之外，無容心矣。所謂天者，非在天之天，吾心之天是也。夫以天下之大，舉而萃之人主之一身，其不能以形爲天下役
translation_en:
…and supreme harmony, far beyond reach and difficult to equal. Those were rulers who communicated the sentiments of high and low, verified the distinction between name and reality, and knew how to make good use of their keen hearing and clear sight. Therefore it is said: "The wisdom of Yao and Shun did not encompass all things; the benevolence of Yao and Shun did not extend love to all people"—because they took drawing close to the worthy as their foremost task. Moreover, I have heard that the ceremonial cap has pendants in front to screen the eyes, and yellow silk plugs to fill the ears so as to block the hearing. Why does it seem as though one should not use keen hearing and clear sight at all? Because possessing them and using them well is how a ruler orders the achievements of enlightened action; setting them aside and not using them is how a ruler nurtures a magnanimous and great substance. These two are cultivated together. Yet securing the hearts of the people and nurturing the lifeblood of the state depend above all on being generous, magnanimous, and sincere. This being so, the ruler's endowment of keen hearing and clear sight relies entirely on being nurtured! Indeed, it relies entirely on being nurtured! This is the meaning that Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) left unexpressed.

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
也較然而徒欲察察焉爲微伺之私智斯勞矣
故不能不寄其耳目於大臣大臣之寄欲其格
吾之非心也而又屑屑焉資其聞見之末智亦
小矣故又不能不養其聰明於己寄其責於人
養其體於己夫然後吾心之天湛然不昧而天
下之輻輳紛至林林總總而莫可紀者舉爲吾
心思之所及心思之所及卽吾耳目之所及也
斯不爲聰明之實而明主之所當務歟人主當
務聰明之實朱子謂任大臣圖國事也請求其
===
所以爲實者究言之書曰惟天聰明惟聖時憲
是君之聰明蓋得之天者也昊天曰明及爾出
王昊天曰旦及爾游衍是天之光明下濟固無
乎不燭矣人君所居天位也所職天職也若禮
樂若刑政若蒸黎若九夷八蠻若鬼神天地若
草木鳥獸其所待於聰明之兼照者至賾且大
以其待照於我者賾且大如此而吾之聰明有
所及有所不及焉非天也天不自用也四時之
吏布其令五行之官宣其氣而天則漠然沖然
punctuated: 也較然。而徒欲察察焉爲微伺之私智，斯勞矣。故不能不寄其耳目於大臣。大臣之寄，欲其格吾之非心也；而又屑屑焉資其聞見之末，智亦小矣。故又不能不養其聰明於己。寄其責於人，養其體於己，夫然後吾心之天湛然不昧，而天下之輻輳紛至、林林總總而莫可紀者，舉爲吾心思之所及。心思之所及，卽吾耳目之所及也。斯不爲聰明之實，而明主之所當務歟？「人主當務聰明之實」，朱子謂任大臣圖國事也。請求其所以爲實者究言之。《書》曰：「惟天聰明，惟聖時憲。」是君之聰明，蓋得之天者也。「昊天曰明，及爾出王；昊天曰旦，及爾游衍。」是天之光明下濟，固無乎不燭矣。人君所居，天位也；所職，天職也。若禮樂，若刑政，若蒸黎，若九夷、八蠻，若鬼神、天地，若草木、鳥獸，其所待於聰明之兼照者至賾且大。以其待照於我者賾且大如此，而吾之聰明有所及、有所不及焉，非天也。天不自用也，四時之吏布其令，五行之官宣其氣，而天則漠然沖然，
translation_en: … is obvious. Yet if he merely wishes to act with petty scrutiny and rely on the private cunning of spying into trifles, this is sheer toil! Therefore, he cannot but entrust his ears and eyes to his great ministers. In entrusting to great ministers, he desires that they rectify the wrong inclinations of his mind; yet if he busies himself with relying on the trivial details of what they hear and see, his wisdom is likewise small. Therefore, he also cannot but nourish his acuity of hearing and sight within himself. By entrusting the responsibilities to others while nourishing the fundamental substance within himself, only then will the Heaven within his mind be limpid and unobscured, and all things in the world that converge in confusion—teeming in multitudes beyond reckoning—will entirely fall within the reach of his thoughts. What his thoughts reach is indeed what his ears and eyes reach. Is this not the reality of acuity of hearing and sight, and that to which an enlightened ruler ought to devote himself? On the saying "The ruler of men ought to devote himself to the reality of acuity of hearing and sight," Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] explained that it means employing great ministers to plan the affairs of state. I beg leave to seek out what constitutes this reality and discuss it exhaustively. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "It is Heaven that is all-intelligent and all-discerning; the sage ruler patterns himself after it." Thus the ruler's acuity of hearing and sight is indeed derived from Heaven. [The Book of Odes says:] "Great Heaven is intelligent, and is with you in all your goings; Great Heaven is clear-seeing, and is with you in your wanderings and indulgences." Thus Heaven's radiant light reaches down below, and there is truly nothing it does not illuminate. The position the ruler occupies is Heaven's position; the office he performs is Heaven's office. Whether rites and music, punishments and governance, the multitude of common people, the Nine Yi and Eight Man tribes, ghosts and spirits, heaven and earth, or plants, trees, birds, and beasts—that which awaits the comprehensive illumination of his acuity of hearing and sight is utmost in complexity and vastness. Given that what awaits illumination from us is so complex and vast, if there are things our acuity of hearing and sight reaches and things it does not reach, then we are not like Heaven. Heaven does not exert itself directly: the officers of the four seasons promulgate its ordinances, the officials of the Five Phases circulate its vital forces, while Heaven itself remains tranquil and serene, …

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
萬物涵於中焉而不能逃其視聽使天莫爲之
宣莫爲之布而欲物物察之亦甚褻矣大臣者
君之四時五行也而爲之君者隘於自用蔽於
偏聽不以大臣鼓其謀而作其哲是以天之所
不能者而責己之必能非天也四時五行天宰
之也上天之載無聲無臭維天之命於穆不已
而後宣者宣布者布故語天道之所以大者不
曰四時五行而必歸之於太虛太虛者聰明之
實也人主之心有天聰天明在焉而壅之則塞
===
蔽之則昏吾自昏且塞其聰明而徒寄之人焉
卽與太虛不相似矣亦非天也惟聰明有所不
及者之非天也則不可有用智之私惟自用而
不用人者之非天也則不可無任相之道惟自
累其心之虛者之非天也則不可不以事天者
事其心是故洛諏焉以洽其聞明試焉以精其
見可以裕吾聰明矣而非其實也有所獻納而
從之有所建立而行之可以資吾聰明矣而非
其實也萋菲之謗不行而聞皆正言忠直之徒
punctuated: 萬物涵於中焉，而不能逃其視聽。使天莫爲之宣，莫爲之布，而欲物物察之，亦甚褻矣。大臣者，君之四時五行也。而爲之君者，隘於自用，蔽於偏聽，不以大臣鼓其謀而作其哲，是以天之所不能者，而責己之必能，非天也。四時五行，天宰之也。「上天之載，無聲無臭」，「維天之命，於穆不已」，而後宣者宣，布者布。故語天道之所以大者，不曰四時五行，而必歸之於太虛。太虛者，聰明之實也。人主之心，有天聰天明在焉，而壅之則塞，蔽之則昏。吾自昏且塞其聰明，而徒寄之人焉，卽與太虛不相似矣，亦非天也。惟聰明有所不及者之非天也，則不可有用智之私；惟自用而不用人者之非天也，則不可無任相之道；惟自累其心之虛者之非天也，則不可不以事天者事其心。是故洛諏焉以洽其聞，明試焉以精其見，可以裕吾聰明矣，而非其實也；有所獻納而從之，有所建立而行之，可以資吾聰明矣，而非其實也；萋菲之謗不行，而聞皆正言，忠直之徒…
translation_en: …all things are encompassed within it and cannot escape its sight and hearing. If Heaven had none to disseminate its vital force and none to proclaim its commands, yet sought to scrutinize every single thing itself, that would be exceedingly undignified. The great ministers are the ruler's four seasons and five agents. Yet when he who is the ruler is narrowed by self-reliance and blinded by partial listening, failing to use his great ministers to rouse their counsels and stir their wisdom, he demands of himself what even Heaven cannot do—and that is not being like Heaven. As for the four seasons and the five agents, it is Heaven that governs them. "The doings of High Heaven have neither sound nor smell," and "The mandate of Heaven, how profound and unceasing it is!"—only thus do those who disseminate, disseminate, and those who proclaim, proclaim. Therefore, when speaking of why the Way of Heaven is great, one does not point to the four seasons and five agents, but must attribute it to the Supreme Void (taixu). The Supreme Void is the substance of keen hearing and clear sight. In the mind of the ruler of men, Heavenly hearing and Heavenly sight reside; yet if obstructed, they become blocked, and if obscured, they grow dim. If I myself dim and block my hearing and sight and merely entrust them to others, I no longer resemble the Supreme Void—and that too is not being like Heaven. Because having anything that one's hearing and sight fail to reach is not being like Heaven, one must not harbor the selfishness of relying on personal cleverness; because relying on oneself and not employing others is not being like Heaven, one must not lack the way of entrusting responsibility to chief ministers; because burdening the emptiness of one's own mind is not being like Heaven, one must serve one's own mind in the very manner that one serves Heaven. Therefore, consulting and inquiring [洛諏, sc. 咨諏] to broaden what one hears, and clearly testing to refine what one sees, can enrich my hearing and sight, yet that is not their true substance. Following whatever counsel is offered, and putting into practice whatever proposal is established, can aid my hearing and sight, yet that is not their true substance. When intricate and malicious slanders do not circulate so that all one hears are upright words, and when loyal and straightforward men…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text: 是任而見諸善行此可以端吾聰明矣而非其 實也恐其聰之察而制恐其明之察而制 之旒固聰明之所收也而未也出有節奏之和 入有箴規之益遠有典籍之稽近有彝訓之考 固聰明之所寄也而猶未也必也於姦聲而遠 之勿使亂耳於邪色而絶之勿使亂目一念之 發至微眇也而視於無形聽於無聲有誠意之 學有慎獨之防有天監在茲之惕日去其所以 壅吾昏吾者而使此心之天洞然不失夫然後 === 天聰之聰聰之實也天明之明明之實也可以 任大臣可以圖國事天下之愁咨不平者吾得 而聰察之天下之闇暗汙濁者吾得而明見之 禮樂若何而脩明刑政若何而振舉烝黎若何 而又安九夷八蠻若何而嚮風天地鬼神若何 而平成而格享草木鳥獸若何而咸若不出堂 陛而四海九州之遠物無遁情不離旦夕而百 千萬年之幾理無遺照天下之人舉曰聰明之 主也後世之人舉曰聰明之主也而莫得其所
punctuated: 是任，而見諸善行，此可以端吾聰明矣，而非其實也。恐其聰之察而制之續，恐其明之察而制之旒，固聰明之所收也，而未也。出有節奏之和，入有箴規之益，遠有典籍之稽，近有彝訓之考，固聰明之所寄也，而猶未也。必也於姦聲而遠之，勿使亂耳；於邪色而絶之，勿使亂目。一念之發，至微眇也，而視於無形，聽於無聲，有誠意之學，有慎獨之防，有天監在茲之惕，日去其所以壅吾、昏吾者，而使此心之天洞然不失，夫然後天聰之聰，聰之實也；天明之明，明之實也。可以任大臣，可以圖國事，天下之愁咨不平者，吾得而聰察之；天下之闇暗汙濁者，吾得而明見之。禮樂若何而脩明？刑政若何而振舉？烝黎若何而乂安？九夷八蠻若何而嚮風？天地鬼神若何而平成、而格享？草木鳥獸若何而咸若？不出堂陛，而四海九州之遠，物無遁情；不離旦夕，而百千萬年之幾，理無遺照。天下之人，舉曰聰明之主也；後世之人，舉曰聰明之主也，而莫得其所
translation_en:
… are employed, and what is seen is all good conduct—this can rectify our hearing and sight, yet it is not their reality. Fearing that one's hearing might be overly prying and thus fashioning ear-plugs of floss [? 恐其聰之察而制], and fearing that one's sight might be overly prying and thus fashioning pendant strings of jade for the crown, are indeed ways to restrain one's hearing and sight, yet this is still not enough. Going out, to have the harmony of ritual cadence; entering in, to have the benefit of admonitions and remonstrances; from afar, to have the examination of canons and records; close at hand, to have the consultation of constant instructions—these are indeed where hearing and sight are lodged, yet even this is still not enough.

Necessary it is that with licentious sounds one keeps them at a distance, not allowing them to disorder the ears; with depraved sights one cuts them off, not allowing them to disorder the eyes. The arising of a single thought is most subtle and minute, yet one sees where there is no form and hears where there is no sound; there is the learning of making the intentions sincere, there is the safeguard of being watchful over oneself when alone, and there is the awe of knowing that "Heaven's inspection is right here." Daily removing whatever blocks us and clouds us, so that the Heaven of this mind remains pellucid and unlost—only then is the hearing of Heaven-gifted hearing the reality of hearing, and the sight of Heaven-gifted sight the reality of sight.

Thus one can entrust Great Ministers and plan the affairs of state. Those in the empire who sigh in distress and suffer injustice, we are able to hear and discern them; what in the empire is dark, obscure, foul, and turbid, we are able to clearly see it. How are ritual and music to be cultivated and made bright? How are punishments and governance to be roused and raised up? How are the multitude of the common people to be brought to order and peace [? 又安]? How are the Nine Yi and Eight Man tribes to be made to turn toward our civilizing influence? How are Heaven and Earth lowered to peace and order, and ghosts and spirits made to arrive and accept offerings? How are grasses, trees, birds, and beasts all made to flourish according to their natures? Without stepping beyond the palace hall and steps, across the distance of the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, no creature can conceal its true condition; without leaving the span of morning and evening, through the subtle springs of a hundred, a thousand, or ten thousand years, no principle escapes illumination. The people of the empire all say, "An acute and clear-sighted sovereign!"; the people of later generations all say, "An acute and clear-sighted sovereign!"—and none can fathom that by which…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
執鞭則以諫說犯君類已故張而大之非
知言也雖然之二子乃若是而後之論者
宜乎其難之矣其他無論即自三晉言之
若霍光之於漢史以小心謹慎稱斷斷然
未有大過人之節行也當昭帝幼沖而上
官昌邑諸臣襲勢而誨亂漢祚移在指顧
間乃光以毅然之氣攝伏羣邪處廢立之
際而舉措甚閑即能擁昭立宣而始元地
節之間漢祚危而復安者皆光之力也光
===
不織視羣小若畜之然至郎有上書脅輒
納之母子賓校劾數言即引用有加假令
充其得受之心漢之圖麟閣者當不在單
于來朝後若溫嶠之於晉史以風儀博學
稱蓋眇然一儒生也晉方草創江左石勒
王敦蘇峻之徒相繼倡亂晉亡在呼吸間
乃嶠以于然之身脫之虎口仗區區忠義
以號呼羣后五州響應即能討石勒劉聰
誅王敦而平蘇峻之難晉之危而復安皆
punctuated: 執鞭，則以諫說犯君類已，故張而大之，非知言也。雖然，之二子乃若是，而後之論者，宜乎其難之矣。其他無論，即自三晉言之，若霍光之於漢，史以小心謹慎稱，斷斷然未有大過人之節行也。當昭帝幼沖，而上官、昌邑諸臣襲勢而誨亂，漢祚移在指顧間。乃光以毅然之氣，攝伏羣邪，處廢立之際而舉措甚閑，即能擁昭立宣，而始元、地節之間，漢祚危而復安者，皆光之力也。光不織，視羣小若畜之。然至郎有上書脅，輒納之；母子賓校劾數言，即引用有加。假令充其得受之心，漢之圖麟閣者，當不在單于來朝後。若溫嶠之於晉，史以風儀博學稱，蓋眇然一儒生也。晉方草創江左，石勒、王敦、蘇峻之徒相繼倡亂，晉亡在呼吸間。乃嶠以于然之身，脫之虎口，仗區區忠義以號呼羣后，五州響應，即能討石勒、劉聰，誅王敦而平蘇峻之難，晉之危而復安，皆
translation_en:
… act as a whip-holder for him, it was because his remonstrating with and offending the ruler resembled his own conduct, and thus he exaggerated and magnified him; this is not truly understanding words. Even so, since those two masters were like this, it is only fitting that later commentators found it difficult to judge. Setting aside other cases, let us speak just from the region of the Three Jin (San Jin 三晉):

Take Huo Guang 霍光 in the Han dynasty: the histories praised him for being scrupulous and cautious, and plainly he did not possess any conduct of integrity vastly surpassing others. Yet when Emperor Zhao 昭帝 was young and tender, and the various ministers of the Shangguan 上官 clan and the Prince of Changyi 昌邑 exploited their power to foment rebellion, the shifting of the Han throne hung on the turn of a hand. Then Guang, with resolute spirit, overawed and subdued the pack of villains; managing the crisis of deposing and enthroning, his measures were utmostly composed. Thus he was able to uphold Emperor Zhao and enthrone Emperor Xuan 宣帝, and during the Shiyuan 始元 (86–80 BCE) and Dijie 地節 (69–66 BCE) eras, that the Han dynasty was imperiled and yet made secure again was all through Guang's strength. Guang was unlearned [?] and regarded the pack of petty men as though herding livestock [?]. Yet when a Court Gentleman (lang 郎) submitted a memorial [concerning those who tried to] coerce him, he readily accepted him; and when Gongsun Ao's [?] retainer and commandant [?] impeached him in a few words, he promoted and employed him with added favor. Suppose he had fully extended this mind capable of accepting criticism, the Han dynasty's painting of portraits in the Unicorn Pavilion (Lin'ge 麟閣) would surely not have waited until after the Chanyu 單于 came to pay court.

Or take Wen Qiao 溫嶠 in the Jin dynasty: the histories praised him for his fine bearing and broad learning—he was, after all, a slight Confucian scholar. When the Jin was just establishing itself in the lower Yangtze region (Jiangzuo 江左), the likes of Shi Le 石勒, Wang Dun 王敦, and Su Jun 蘇峻 successively instigated rebellions, and the fall of the Jin hung on a single breath. Yet Qiao, with his lone person, escaped from the tiger's jaws, and relying on his modest loyalty and righteousness, cried out to the various regional lords. Five provinces responded like an echo, and he was thus able to campaign against Shi Le and Liu Cong 劉聰, execute Wang Dun, and pacify the rebellion of Su Jun. That the Jin was imperiled and yet made secure again was all…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
墳籍一遇李膺而名稱籍籍滿天下史稱
林宗雅俗無所失將其明性特有主之者
乎蓋言學也逵方改務不惟自晦恂恂善
道天下士咸慕之以成名世之稱者曰郭
林宗何如人蓋誠異之也王仲淹陳隋間
所稱至人也當其自博士公受元經巳能
知治亂之故而至從今育之徒游遂慨然
有四方之志史稱退志其道而六經大就
聖人之旨天下之能事畢矣蓋言學也動
===
稽古則洵有格言豪傑多所嚮應自以王
佐之術相授受後之稱者曰仲淹古之隱
德君子蓋誠異之也夫辦天下之事易成
天下之事難處危急之時易處紆緩之時
難爲才而才不爲器而器天下之人指而稱
曰是非才人也是非器人也是目論矣然
亦有當繁劇紛擾而中不亂當移游成敗
而中不變才不必名也器不必名也則必
有所以主張是者學是也夫學以資才非
punctuated: 墳籍，一遇李膺，而名稱籍籍滿天下。史稱林宗雅俗無所失，將其明性特有主之者乎？蓋言學也。逵方改務，不惟自晦，恂恂善道，天下士咸慕之以成名。世之稱者曰：「郭林宗何如人？」蓋誠異之也。王仲淹，陳、隋間所稱至人也。當其自博士公受《元經》，巳能知治亂之故；而至從今育之徒游，遂慨然有四方之志。史稱退志其道，而六經大就，聖人之旨、天下之能事畢矣，蓋言學也。動稽古則，洵有格言，豪傑多所嚮應，自以王佐之術相授受。後之稱者曰：「仲淹，古之隱德君子。」蓋誠異之也。夫辦天下之事易，成天下之事難；處危急之時易，處紆緩之時難。爲才而才，不爲器而器，天下之人指而稱曰：「是非才人也，是非器人也。」是目論矣。然亦有當繁劇紛擾而中不亂，當移游成敗而中不變，才不必名也，器不必名也，則必有所以主張是者，學是也。夫學以資才，非
translation_en: … ancient texts; once he met Li Ying 李膺, his reputation spread far and wide throughout the empire. The histories state that Linzong 林宗 [Guo Tai 郭泰] never failed in dealing with either the refined or the vulgar—was it not because his luminous nature had something special governing it? Indeed, this refers to his learning. When paths were blocked and affairs changed [?], he did not merely conceal himself in obscurity, but sincerely and gently guided others in the good way, so that scholars across the empire all admired him and through him established their reputations. When people of the world praised him, saying, "What kind of man is Guo Linzong!", they truly marveled at him. Wang Zhongyan 王仲淹 [Wang Tong 王通] was someone acclaimed during the Chen and Sui dynasties as a man of supreme attainment. When he received the Primal Classic (Yuanjing 元經) from his father the Erudite, he was already able to understand the causes of order and disorder; and when he went on to study with men such as令育 [Linghu Defen 令狐德棻? / Liu炫?][?], he was stirred with ambition to bring order to the four quarters. The histories state that when he withdrew to set his mind upon his Way, his work on the Six Classics was brought to great completion, exhausting the purport of the sages and all the capabilities of the world—indeed, this refers to his learning. In every action he examined ancient models, truly producing maxims of conduct; outstanding heroes responded to him in great numbers, and they transmitted the arts of assisting a true king to one another. When later generations praised him, saying, "Zhongyan was a gentleman of hidden virtue of the ancient type," they truly marveled at him. Now, to manage the affairs of the world is easy, but to bring the affairs of the world to completion is difficult; to deal with times of crisis and urgency is easy, but to deal with times of calm and leisure is difficult. If one acts for the sake of talent and shows talent, or does not act for the sake of capacity and yet shows capacity [?], and the people of the world point and say, "Is this not a man of talent? Is this not a man of capacity?", that is merely superficial judgment. Yet there are also those who, when facing complex tasks and tumultuous disorder, remain unperturbed within, and when facing shifting circumstances [?] of success and failure, remain unchanged within; their talent need not be famed, and their capacity need not be famed, for there must be something that governs them—and that is learning. Now, learning serves to nourish talent, not…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
以用才學以弘器非以貫器管晏不足爲
曾西氏已志之矣若晉之數子其才其器
與管晏孰優劣要當有以辨之迺其學如
林宗仲淹者果孔孟之遺乎使與數子論
建立果相肖似乎抑亦有出數子之上者
乎無乃當漢隋之間時不可爲而依託爲
自全計乎則二子之學未易優也雖然學
貫於知道知道則雲行雨施其機不露知
道則天淵定其局不張不露則發之若
===
硎刃手不可拭也不張則容之若武庫目
不可應接也以才器運天下而天下不知
才不知器而才器之效收之自我此經世
之學也區區求爲名高而招致一時之俊
以自侈門戶其於學則何如
第四問
李弘道
同考試官教諭張　批〔經畫時務如指掌蓋救弊補偏之略素定於中者信能行此晉無難事矣〕
punctuated:
以用才，學以弘器，非以貫器。管、晏不足爲，曾西氏已志之矣。若晉之數子，其才其器與管、晏孰優劣，要當有以辨之。迺其學如林宗、仲淹者，果孔、孟之遺乎？使與數子論建立，果相肖似乎？抑亦有出數子之上者乎？無乃當漢、隋之間，時不可爲，而依託爲自全計乎？則二子之學，未易優也。雖然，學貫於知道。知道則雲行雨施，其機不露；知道則天淵定，其局不張。不露則發之若硎刃，手不可拭也；不張則容之若武庫，目不可應接也。以才器運天下，而天下不知才、不知器，而才器之效收之自我，此經世之學也。區區求爲名高，而招致一時之俊以自侈門戶，其於學則何如？

第四問
李弘道
同考試官教諭張批〔經畫時務如指掌，蓋救弊補偏之略素定於中者。信能行此，晉無難事矣。〕
translation_en:
…for merely employing talent; learning is to broaden one's capacity, not merely to string capacities together [?]. That Guan Zhong 管仲 and Yan Ying 晏嬰 were not worth emulating, Zeng Xi 曾西 had already noted. As for those several worthies of Shanxi (Jin 晉), whether their talent and capacity were superior or inferior to those of Guan and Yan must be discerned. Yet as for learning such as that of Guo Tai 郭泰 (courtesy name Linzong 林宗) and Wang Tong 王通 (courtesy name Zhongyan 仲淹)—was it truly the legacy of Confucius and Mencius? If one were to discuss actual achievements with those several worthies, would they really resemble one another, or would they surpass those several worthies? Or could it be that during the late Han and Sui periods, when the times did not allow for action, they merely used scholarly discourse as a pretext for self-preservation? In that case, the learning of these two masters cannot easily be judged superior. Nevertheless, learning is unified by knowing the Way (or: learning places its highest value on knowing the Way [貫 for 貴?]). When one knows the Way, it is like clouds moving and rain falling, its subtle mechanism never exposed; when one knows the Way, heaven and the abyss are settled in their places, its framework never ostentatiously displayed. Because it is not exposed, when it is unleashed it is like a blade fresh from the whetstone that cannot be wiped by hand; because it is not ostentatiously displayed, what it contains is like an armory whose contents the eye cannot take in all at once. To move the world through talent and capacity while the world remains unaware of that talent and unaware of that capacity, yet reaping the effects of talent and capacity oneself—this is the learning of statecraft. As for pettily seeking lofty fame and gathering the outstanding talents of the age merely to boast of one's own faction, how does that compare as learning?

Fourth Policy Question
Li Hongdao 李弘道
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu 教諭) Zhang comments: [He plans out current affairs as clearly as pointing to his own palm; clearly his strategies for remedying abuses and correcting imbalances have long been settled within his mind. If these can truly be put into practice, there will be no difficult matters left in Shanxi.]

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授譚　批〔條對詳明文詞古健〕
考試官教授劉　批〔儁傑之識〕
天下之計有可爲數十年計者有不可爲
朝夕計者夫天下時而已時之所趣若流
不能障而塞之也我不能爲時而能不違
時恃有以應之也天下之事惟時之使非
以窮我也而調停均節審其機宜以應之
不繆於拘攣不濫於流移是我之所以用
時也我能用時數十年不論也朝夕不論
===
也請以局喻局至變也局之譜靈無類千
百種局若此應若彼曾未有一類其機宜
在人不在局譜故也議法者何以異於是
夫議法亦有說議於有餘之中者易議於
不足之中者難議昔之不足者易議今之
不足者難蓋變屢出而爲所窮時爲之矣
今晉之當亟議者有四而本末有以應之
自
藩封之典盛而祿食于土者亦既衆矣郡生
punctuated:
考試官教授譚　批〔條對詳明，文詞古健。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔儁傑之識。〕
天下之計，有可爲數十年計者，有不可爲朝夕計者。夫天下，時而已。時之所趣若流，不能障而塞之也。我不能爲時，而能不違時，恃有以應之也。天下之事，惟時之使，非以窮我也；而調停均節，審其機宜以應之，不繆於拘攣，不濫於流移，是我之所以用時也。我能用時，數十年不論也，朝夕不論也。請以局喻：局至變也，局之譜靈無類，千百種局若此，應若彼，曾未有一類，其機宜在人不在局譜故也。議法者何以異於是？夫議法亦有說：議於有餘之中者易，議於不足之中者難；議昔之不足者易，議今之不足者難。蓋變屢出而爲所窮，時爲之矣。今晉之當亟議者有四，而本末有以應之。自藩封之典盛，而祿食于土者亦既衆矣。郡生
translation_en:
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Tan comments: [The itemized responses are detailed and clear; the diction and style are archaic and vigorous.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu comments: [The insight of an outstanding talent.]
In planning for the empire, there are plans that can be made for several decades, and there are plans that cannot even be made for a single morning or evening. Now, the empire is simply a matter of the times. The trend of the times is like a flowing current; one cannot dike it up or block it. We cannot create the times, yet we can avoid going against the times, relying on having the means to respond to them. The affairs of the empire are driven solely by the times, not in order to drive us to exhaustion; and to harmonize, adjust, and evenly regulate them, examining their critical opportunities and contingencies so as to respond to them—neither erring through rigid constraint nor overflowing into aimless drift—this is how we make use of the times. If we are able to make use of the times, it does not matter whether it is for several decades, nor does it matter whether it is for a single morning or evening. Please allow me to use a game of strategy as an analogy: a game on the board is supremely changeable, and the manuals for the board are ingeniously varied beyond categorization. Among hundreds and thousands of configurations, when the board is like this, one responds like that, and never is there a single fixed category, because the critical opportunities and contingencies lie with the person and not with the board manuals. How is deliberating on laws and policies any different from this? Now, in deliberating on laws there is also an explanation: deliberating amidst abundance is easy, whereas deliberating amidst insufficiency is difficult; deliberating on the insufficiency of the past is easy, whereas deliberating on the insufficiency of the present is difficult. This is because changes repeatedly arise and one is driven to exhaustion by them; the times have brought this about. Today, in Shanxi (Jin), there are four matters that ought to be urgently deliberated upon, and in both fundamentals and incidentals there are means to respond to them. Ever since the institution of enfeoffing imperial princes flourished, those who draw stipends from the land have already become numerous. The princely descendants of the commanderies [?] multiply and…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
養益繁民之入不足以供
宗藩之需之所出加之師旅凶荒而三晉常
患於無祿自兼併之計肆而屯田之沒於
豪强者亦旣盛矣矧依假冊籍陽應其名
而陰收其地利加之招納亡命之徒而三
晉常患於無屯自計羨之議起而課無積
藏池之生不生不可必朝三暮四之術要
惟足課此可爲一二年計也加之屢年浸
沒而三晉常患於無鹽自改戶之風熾而
===
軍無定籍軍之正與僞不足論而被出此
入要惟實伍此但可以充目前文具也加
之窮邊改調而三晉常患於無軍今下之
所以游談聚議上之所以變政易令以應
四者之變不可勝數矣而祿終不支屯終
不清鹽終不權軍終不實是豈眞不可應
也無亦拘攣其說不能隨所趣而以時應
之耳夫局不變而移譜譜不變而移人固
矣亦有信變而之譜信譜而忘局者今晉
punctuated: 養益繁，民之入不足以供宗藩之需之所出，加之師旅凶荒，而三晉常患於無祿。自兼併之計肆，而屯田之沒於豪强者亦旣盛矣。矧依假冊籍，陽應其名而陰收其地利，加之招納亡命之徒，而三晉常患於無屯。自計羨之議起，而課無積藏。池之生不生不可必，朝三暮四之術，要惟足課，此可爲一二年計也。加之屢年浸沒，而三晉常患於無鹽。自改戶之風熾，而軍無定籍。軍之正與僞不足論，而被出此入，要惟實伍，此但可以充目前文具也。加之窮邊改調，而三晉常患於無軍。今下之所以游談聚議，上之所以變政易令，以應四者之變，不可勝數矣，而祿終不支、屯終不清、鹽終不權、軍終不實。是豈眞不可應也？無亦拘攣其說，不能隨所趣而以時應之耳。夫局不變而移譜，譜不變而移人，固矣；亦有信變而之譜，信譜而忘局者，今晉
translation_en: … have multiplied and their upkeep has grown ever more burdensome, so the revenue from the common people is insufficient to meet the expenditures required for the imperial clansmen and princely establishments. Added to this are military campaigns and famines, so that the Three Jin region [Shanxi] constantly suffers from a lack of stipends. Ever since schemes of land engrossment have run rampant, the confiscation of military state-farm lands (tuntian) by powerful magnates has already become widespread. Moreover, they rely on falsified registers, outwardly answering to the nominal quotas while secretly reaping the profits of the land; added to this is their harboring of fugitives and desperadoes, so that the Three Jin region constantly suffers from a lack of state farms. Ever since proposals for calculating surplus revenues arose, the salt tax has had no accumulated reserves. Whether the salt ponds produce or not cannot be guaranteed; through "three in the morning and four at night" stopgap trickery, the sole aim is merely to meet the tax quota—a policy that can serve as a plan for only a year or two. Added to this are repeated years of flooding and ruin, so that the Three Jin region constantly suffers from a lack of salt. Ever since the practice of altering household registrations grew rampant, the military has lacked fixed registers. Whether soldiers are genuine or replacements is no longer even worth discussing; shifting men out there [reading 被 as 彼?] and bringing them in here with the sole aim of filling the ranks can only serve as a paper formality for the present moment. Added to this are redeployments to the remote frontiers, so that the Three Jin region constantly suffers from a lack of soldiers. Today, the casual talk and gathered deliberations of those below, and the altering of policies and changing of ordinances by those above in order to respond to changes in these four matters, are beyond counting. Yet in the end, stipends remain unsustainable, state farms remain uncleared, the salt monopoly [reading 權 for 榷] remains unregulated, and the military ranks remain unfilled. Is it truly that these problems cannot be met? Or is it not rather that people are bound by their rigid theories and are unable to follow the trend of events and respond to them in accordance with the times? Now, to shift the manual when the game-board situation does not change, or to shift the player when the manual does not change, is certainly obstinate; yet there are also those who believe in change and yet resort to manuals, or believe in manuals and forget the actual board situation. Is not the present [situation of] Jin…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
不足中也哉
國家計軍授田蓋畜之也晉疆子粒不支半
軍不支必枵腹不任指使指使不任而誅
呼繼之非所以稱其畜也其後必當惟稽
其子粒間有侵奪者視地而補之軍傚漢
塞下渭濵故事與軍共之分種之利既博
而收利者惟取盈則不必清丈而軍皆土
著矣不然分晝晉疆不能一朝辦而欺愚
羸縮不可計矣夫晉之鹽古稱曰海眼蓋
===
以自生而易利也鹽之生不生視水之高
下中條之麓其山溜未易洩也鹽不花數
年矣此不足之尤者也不惟輕販無賴之
徒不可羈而撈收之編役且坐困頃者水
漸落而鹵且生則水猶可禦也或傚禦海
之計而以應目前之需則不必峻法取盈
異日者冀一生則年計所積必倍不必拘
計羨間矣夫晉兵古曰天下莫强蓋以習
邊而輕敵也軍之籍不籍視貲之盈縮所
punctuated: 不足中也哉？國家計軍授田，蓋畜之也。晉疆子粒不支半，軍不支必枵腹不任指使；指使不任而誅呼繼之，非所以稱其畜也。其後必當惟稽其子粒，間有侵奪者，視地而補之軍，傚漢塞下、渭濵故事，與軍共之。分種之利既博，而收利者惟取盈，則不必清丈，而軍皆土著矣。不然，分晝晉疆不能一朝辦，而欺愚、羸縮不可計矣。夫晉之鹽，古稱曰「海眼」，蓋以自生而易利也。鹽之生不生，視水之高下。中條之麓，其山溜未易洩也，鹽不花數年矣，此不足之尤者也。不惟輕販無賴之徒不可羈，而撈收之編役且坐困。頃者水漸落而鹵且生，則水猶可禦也。或傚禦海之計，而以應目前之需，則不必峻法取盈。異日者冀一生，則年計所積必倍，不必拘計羨間矣。夫晉兵，古曰「天下莫强」，蓋以習邊而輕敵也。軍之籍不籍，視貲之盈縮。所
translation_en:
…not suffice to hit the mark?

When the state calculated the number of soldiers and allotted them fields, its purpose was to nourish them. In the territory of Shanxi (Jin 晉), the grain tax from military farms does not cover even half the need. When soldiers are not supported, they will inevitably go hungry and be unfit to take orders; if they are unfit to take orders and yet demands and exactions follow closely upon them, this is no way to fulfill the aim of nourishing them. Hereafter, one ought simply to audit the grain tax yield, and where lands have occasionally been encroached upon or seized, inspect the land and make it up to the soldiers—following the Han-dynasty precedents along the frontier and the banks of the Wei River (Weibin 渭濵) by sharing the land with the troops. Once the benefits of shared cultivation are broad and those who collect the returns seek only to meet the quota, there will be no need for a cadastral resurvey, and the soldiers will all become settled locals. Otherwise, demarcating [分晝 for 分畫] the territory of Shanxi cannot be accomplished in a single morning, and the deception of the ignorant as well as the shortfalls and surpluses will be beyond calculation.

Now the salt of Shanxi was in antiquity called the "Eye of the Sea" (Haiyan 海眼), because it crystallized of itself and readily yielded profit. Whether the salt forms or not depends on the rise and fall of the water level. At the foot of Mount Zhongtiao (中條), the mountain runoff is not easily drained away, so the salt has failed to crystallize into flowers for several years now; this is an extreme case of insufficiency. Not only can the reckless, shiftless smugglers not be reined in, but the registered corvée laborers assigned to harvest the salt are left sitting in distress. Recently the floodwaters have gradually receded and the brine is about to form salt, showing that the water can still be diked off. If we perhaps imitate the methods used for diking the sea in order to meet immediate needs, we will not need harsh laws to force full quotas. In the future, should we hope for a single full crystallization, the annual accumulation will surely double, and there will be no need to be bound by calculations of surplus margins.

Now as for the soldiers of Shanxi, in antiquity it was said that "none in the world are stronger," because they were accustomed to the frontier and made light of the enemy. Whether soldiers remain on the registers or not depends on the abundance or scarcity of their provisions and funds. Where…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
餉之交其去留未易覊也軍之虛籍亦數
年矣此不足之尤者也不惟隱避滑稽之
徒不可窮而里胥之役益張熾頂者軍資
費而邊民困則軍猶可募也或倣招募之
議以充塞下則不必窮句盡類異日者冀
其習利則邊民樂戰不必句攝而塞下皆
勝兵矣夫事不必有成計惟在當機機不
必有定執惟在善收夫所謂收者數十年
之利害不以小小不便而止朝夕之計不以
===
小利而爭趣無可成之狀而不可成之形
已見無可議之端而議者已踵其後無惑
乎收之難也收之難則法不一法不一則
爲三晉計者窮毋乃漫不知收與雖然天
下之法何常亦權之以人而已夫所謂人
者以其用時也防禁之大深督責之大急
非時也用時者至嚴而有所至寛至易而
有所至險使天下信之而不測惟曰此利
我也不知我有以制其後則我之用彼適
punctuated: 餉之交，其去留未易覊也。軍之虛籍亦數年矣，此不足之尤者也。不惟隱避滑稽之徒不可窮，而里胥之役益張熾。頂者軍資費而邊民困，則軍猶可募也。或倣招募之議以充塞下，則不必窮句盡類。異日者冀其習利，則邊民樂戰，不必句攝，而塞下皆勝兵矣。夫事不必有成計，惟在當機；機不必有定執，惟在善收。夫所謂收者，數十年之利害，不以小小不便而止；朝夕之計，不以小利而爭趣。無可成之狀，而不可成之形已見；無可議之端，而議者已踵其後，無惑乎收之難也。收之難則法不一，法不一則爲三晉計者窮，毋乃漫不知收與？雖然，天下之法何常，亦權之以人而已。夫所謂人者，以其用時也。防禁之大深，督責之大急，非時也。用時者，至嚴而有所至寛，至易而有所至險。使天下信之而不測，惟曰：「此利我也。」不知我有以制其後，則我之用彼，適…
translation_en:
…intersection of their provisioning, their desertion or remaining is not easily restrained. The military registers have also been filled with phantom names for several years now, which is an extreme case of deficiency. Not only can the evasive and cunning fellows not be tracked down exhaustively, but the impositions of village functionaries and petty clerks grow ever more rampant. Recently [reading 頂 as 頃], military funds are expended while the frontier people are distressed, which means soldiers can still be recruited. If we were to imitate the proposals for recruitment in order to fill the frontier defenses, then there would be no need to exhaustively draft and round up every category of household. In the future, hoping that they become accustomed to the benefits, the frontier people will gladly fight; there will be no need to forcibly draft them, and the frontier defenses will be filled with victorious troops.

Now, affairs do not necessarily have a pre-established plan; everything lies in meeting the opportunity. Opportunities do not necessarily have a fixed rule to cling to; everything lies in knowing how to bring things to fruition. What is meant by bringing things to fruition is that regarding the advantages and harms of several decades, one does not stop because of minor inconveniences; regarding the plans of morning and evening, one does not scramble after petty profits. When before there is any sign of success, the appearance of failure is already visible, and before there is any ground for criticism, critics are already following on one's heels—it is no wonder that bringing things to fruition is difficult! When bringing things to fruition is difficult, the laws are not unified; when the laws are not unified, those who make plans for the Three Jin [Shanxi] are driven to exhaustion. Could it be that they casually fail to understand how to bring things to fruition?

Even so, what constancy is there in the laws of the realm? They are simply weighed and adapted by men. What is meant by "men" is that they make use of the times. When prohibitions are too deep and reproofs and demands are too urgent, it is out of step with the times. Those who make use of the times are utmost in strictness yet have points of utmost leniency; they are utmost in easiness yet have points of utmost peril. They cause the realm to trust them without being able to fathom them, saying only, "This benefits us," not knowing that we have the means to control what comes after. Thus, our making use of them is precisely…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
所以用時也惟能用時則不患不收不收惟
收則數十年朝夕之計若指畫然此局論
也
第五問
蕭三善
同考試官學正姜　批〔不計虜勢强弱惟先自治且歸〕
考試官教授譚　批〔肯綮可見之行〕
考試官教授劉　批〔暢諳要務〕
===
重任將得禦夷上策者
夫中國之制夷非曰大懲創之使折北而
不支也又非曰設約而固要之使必柔服
而不貳也吾脩內治飭外防使外有難犯
之形內有不可不勝之實則虜之强弱吾
直眇焉視之即款關納貢稽首稱藩不爲
喜雖鳴鏑飲馬飛羽燔燧不爲懼隨其叛
服去來常有以應之則中國之勢重勢重
則機在我夫使中國勢重而機在我是長
勝之筭善之善者也法曰先爲不可勝以
punctuated:
所以用時也。惟能用時，則不患不收。不收惟收，則數十年朝夕之計，若指畫然。此局論也。

第五問
蕭三善
同考試官學正姜　批〔不計虜勢强弱，惟先自治，且歸〕重任將，得禦夷上策者。
考試官教授譚　批〔肯綮可見之行。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔暢諳要務。〕

夫中國之制夷，非曰大懲創之，使折北而不支也；又非曰設約而固要之，使必柔服而不貳也。吾脩內治，飭外防，使外有難犯之形，內有不可不勝之實，則虜之强弱，吾直眇焉視之。即款關納貢，稽首稱藩，不爲喜；雖鳴鏑飲馬，飛羽燔燧，不爲懼。隨其叛服去來，常有以應之，則中國之勢重；勢重則機在我。夫使中國勢重而機在我，是長勝之筭，善之善者也。《法》曰：「先爲不可勝，以
translation_en:
… is precisely how to make use of the times. Only when one can make use of the times will there be no worry about failing to gather things in. Once they are gathered in [?], the plans worked out morning and evening over several decades will be as clear as if traced out with a finger. This is the conclusion of the matter.

Question Five
Xiao Sanshan 蕭三善
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Jiang 姜, comments: 〔Disregarding whether the caitiffs' power is strong or weak, he focuses first on self-governance, and furthermore places〕 heavy responsibility on the generals, thereby grasping the supreme strategy for defending against the barbarians.
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Tan 譚, comments: 〔Hits the crucial points and can be put into actual practice.〕
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉, comments: 〔Fluent and well-versed in essential affairs.〕

Now, for the Central State to control the barbarians does not mean inflicting a great chastisement upon them so that they are routed and unable to hold out; nor does it mean establishing treaties and firmly binding them so that they are sure to submit meekly and never be duplicitous. If we cultivate our internal governance and put our external defenses in order, causing the exterior to present a form difficult to violate and the interior to possess the reality of inevitable victory [?], then as for the strength or weakness of the caitiffs, we may simply regard it as negligible. Even if they knock at the passes to offer tribute, bowing their heads to the ground and declaring themselves vassals, we do not rejoice; even if they shoot whistling arrows and water their horses, sending feathered dispatches flying and lighting beacon fires, we do not fear. Responding constantly to them according to their rebellion or submission, their departure or arrival, the strategic position of the Central State will carry weight; when its strategic position carries weight, the initiative rests with us. Now, causing the strategic position of the Central State to carry weight and the initiative to rest with us is the calculation for enduring victory, the best of the best. The Art of War (Fa) says: "First make yourself invincible, in order to…"

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
待敵之可勝其謂是乎夫制夷無上策自
古難之矣即漢諸臣運籌策而賛廟謨言
人人殊約其要歸兩科而巳故曰縉紳之
儒則守和親介胄之士則言征伐蓋其槩
也故有強而戰者亦有強而不戰者有弱
而和者亦有弱而不和者屈伸與變機勢
相反總之非乘利則用餌也以今視昔鑑
戒較然在智者遠覽而用之當耳夫晉苦
虜患久矣惟我
===
穆宗皇帝威亶中外臣服四夷既巳納北虜之
貢而聽其市今三歲矣無論諸邊即耳目
之所睹記父兄緩帶稚子咽哺何其安也
雖恣求數數計所省不啻鉅萬云斯非餌
以羈縻之明效與說者謂虜近塞城城疑
爲紿我疑之非過也獨不憶中行說爲虜
畫策乎其實虜之備我亦猶我之備虜而
不知彼之備固彼之忌也無乃贅疣之類
與夫猛獸在原野至虓嚂也然可驅在柙
punctuated: 待敵之可勝」，其謂是乎！夫制夷無上策，自古難之矣。即漢諸臣運籌策而賛廟謨，言人人殊，約其要，歸兩科而巳。故曰：「縉紳之儒則守和親，介胄之士則言征伐。」蓋其槩也。故有強而戰者，亦有強而不戰者；有弱而和者，亦有弱而不和者。屈伸與變，機勢相反，總之非乘利則用餌也。以今視昔，鑑戒較然，在智者遠覽而用之當耳。夫晉苦虜患久矣。惟我穆宗皇帝威亶中外，臣服四夷，既巳納北虜之貢而聽其市，今三歲矣。無論諸邊，即耳目之所睹記，父兄緩帶，稚子咽哺，何其安也！雖恣求數數，計所省不啻鉅萬云。斯非餌以羈縻之明效與？說者謂虜近塞城城，疑爲紿我。疑之非過也，獨不憶中行說爲虜畫策乎？其實虜之備我，亦猶我之備虜。而不知彼之備固彼之忌也，無乃贅疣之類與？夫猛獸在原野，至虓嚂也；然可驅在柙，
translation_en: … await the enemy's vulnerability to defeat." Does it not refer to this? Now, in controlling the barbarians there is no supreme strategy; since antiquity it has been considered difficult. Even when the various ministers of the Han devised strategies and assisted in the court's counsels, everyone's words differed, yet if we summarize their essentials, they came down to only two categories. Thus it was said: "Girdled Confucian scholars hold fast to peace and kinship, while armored warriors speak of punitive expeditions." This is the general outline. Therefore, there were those who were strong and fought, and also those who were strong and did not fight; there were those who were weak and made peace, and also those who were weak and did not make peace. Yielding and advancing along with changing circumstances, the opportunities and situations were opposite to one another; in short, if it was not taking advantage of strategic gain, then it was using bait. Viewing the past from the present, the mirror of warning is clear; it lies only in the wise taking a far-sighted view and applying it appropriately. Now, Jin [Shanxi] has suffered from the caitiff [Mongol] menace for a long time. Only through our Emperor Muzong, whose majesty inspired awe at home and abroad and brought the four barbarian peoples into submission, have we already accepted tribute from the northern caitiffs and permitted their border markets, which has now been three years. Not to mention all the frontiers, just from what our own eyes and ears have witnessed and remembered, fathers and elder brothers loosen their belts in ease while young children are fed in peace—how tranquil it is! Even though they make arbitrary demands repeatedly, when we calculate what has been saved, it is no less than tens of millions. Is this not the clear efficacy of using bait to keep them under loose rein (jimi)? Commentators say that the caitiffs are building walled enclosures [?] near the frontier passes, suspecting that they are deceiving us. To suspect them is not excessive, but do they alone not recall Zhonghang Yue devising strategies for the caitiffs? In truth, the caitiffs' guarding against us is just like our guarding against the caitiffs. Yet to not know that their preparations are indeed born of their own fear—is that not like treating it as a mere superfluous excrescence? Now, when a fierce beast is in the open wilderness, it is utmost in its roaring ferocity; yet it can be driven into a cage, …

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
或逸而出猶能以機焉反之何者貪於餌
也今之制虜何以異是雖然和不可恃備
不可忘請以漢喻蓋武帝未嘗一日忘匈
奴選將出塞數矣單于僅僅遠走亡匿幕
北至宣帝之世乃始稽首臣服遣子入侍
以五單于爭立壞亂幾亡武帝餘威有以
懾之而武帝又承文景之後其富庶有足
賴者焉以古爲鑑參伍彼已則北虜之和
也果將信之與抑將激之與不則亦將備
之與有疆場之責者可以權矣夫所謂備
云者非如武帝輕於黷武也又非如宣帝
必欲降虜也不過即
===
廟堂之所指畫者劑量而潤澤之耳故險隘
議脩矣而城堡弗併我之所備者衆而力
分非計也盍亦併小堡以成大堡乎如是
則我專爲一虜分爲十所與戰者約以衆
待寡一策也胡馬議收矣而車戰弗講以
所短角所長非計也盍亦改步兵以脩戰
punctuated: 或逸而出，猶能以機焉反之，何者？貪於餌也。今之制虜，何以異是？雖然，和不可恃，備不可忘。請以漢喻：蓋武帝未嘗一日忘匈奴，選將出塞數矣，單于僅僅遠走，亡匿幕北；至宣帝之世，乃始稽首臣服，遣子入侍。以五單于爭立，壞亂幾亡，武帝餘威有以懾之，而武帝又承文、景之後，其富庶有足賴者焉。以古爲鑑，參伍彼己，則北虜之和也，果將信之與？抑將激之與？不則亦將備之與？有疆場之責者，可以權矣。夫所謂備云者，非如武帝輕於黷武也，又非如宣帝必欲降虜也，不過即廟堂之所指畫者，劑量而潤澤之耳。故險隘議脩矣，而城堡弗併，我之所備者衆而力分，非計也。盍亦併小堡以成大堡乎？如是，則我專爲一，虜分爲十，所與戰者約，以衆待寡，一策也。胡馬議收矣，而車戰弗講，以所短角所長，非計也。盍亦改步兵以脩戰
translation_en:
… Should it escape and break out, one can still bring it back by means of a trap. Why is this? Because it is greedy for the bait. How is our present control of the northern caitiffs any different from this?

Even so, peace cannot be relied upon, and preparedness must not be forgotten. Allow me to use the Han dynasty as an analogy. Emperor Wu (Wudi) never for a single day forgot the Xiongnu, and he repeatedly selected generals to march beyond the frontier passes; yet the Chanyu merely fled far away to hide north of the desert. Only in the reign of Emperor Xuan (Xuandi) did the Xiongnu first bow their heads in submission as vassals and send their sons to attend the court as hostages. Because five Chanyus were contending for the throne, they fell into ruinous disorder and nearly perished; the lingering awe of Emperor Wu was enough to cow them, and Emperor Wu had moreover inherited the legacy of Emperors Wen and Jing, whose wealth and populousness provided a sufficient foundation on which to rely.

If we take antiquity as a mirror and compare their situation and ours, then regarding this peace with the northern caitiffs: shall we truly trust it? Or shall we provoke them? Or, if not, shall we prepare against them? Those who bear responsibility for the frontiers can weigh this carefully.

Now, what is meant by "preparedness" is not lightly engaging in militarism like Emperor Wu, nor is it insisting on forcing the caitiffs to surrender like Emperor Xuan; it is nothing more than taking the plans directed by the imperial court, adjusting their measure, and refining their execution. Thus, repairing strategic passes has been discussed, yet walled forts have not been consolidated; when the places we must defend are numerous, our strength is divided, which is not a sound plan. Why not consolidate small forts to form large forts? In that case, our forces will be concentrated as one while the caitiffs are divided into ten; those with whom we engage will be few, and awaiting the few with the many is one strategy. Acquiring barbarian horses has been discussed, yet chariot warfare is not practiced; pitting our weakness against their strength is not a sound plan. Why not adapt our infantry to build war…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
卒畏將勇敢倡則勇于公戰邊民寬則人
懷土情無外洩自是虜尋吾盟我則開誠
撫綏不為利而誘之不乘亂而取之自是
虜背吾盟我則因利制權或閉關以謝之
或移師以討之是和可也戰亦可也以之
備山大可也以之備各鎮亦可也蓋機常
在我應變有餘而虜之强弱叛服不與焉
所謂脩內治飭外防先為不可勝以待敵
之可勝者此也抑又有說焉昔者趙之良
===
將李牧常居代鴈門備匈奴其地固今之
山大一隅耳考其時猶能具選車得千三
百乘騎相埒百金之士五萬人彀者倍之
而又日椎牛享士卒能出奇大破殺匈奴
十餘萬騎滅襜襤破東胡降林胡單于遯
走不敢近趙邊者數年此無他任之專而
彼得以盡其才也然則
今日重專閫之選弛文法之禁唯在
將將者一加之意耳
punctuated: 卒畏將；勇敢倡，則勇于公戰；邊民寬，則人懷土，情無外洩。自是虜尋吾盟，我則開誠撫綏，不為利而誘之，不乘亂而取之；自是虜背吾盟，我則因利制權，或閉關以謝之，或移師以討之。是和可也，戰亦可也；以之備山、大可也，以之備各鎮亦可也。蓋機常在我，應變有餘，而虜之强弱叛服不與焉。所謂「脩內治，飭外防，先為不可勝以待敵之可勝」者，此也。抑又有說焉：昔者趙之良將李牧，常居代、鴈門備匈奴，其地固今之山、大一隅耳。考其時，猶能具選車得千三百乘，騎相埒，百金之士五萬人，彀者倍之，而又日椎牛享士，卒能出奇，大破殺匈奴十餘萬騎，滅襜襤，破東胡，降林胡，單于遯走，不敢近趙邊者數年。此無他，任之專而彼得以盡其才也。然則今日重專閫之選，弛文法之禁，唯在將將者一加之意耳。
translation_en: … the soldiers will stand in awe of their generals; when bravery is encouraged, they will fight courageously in public battles; when the frontier populace is treated leniently, people will cherish their homeland and intelligence will not leak out to the enemy. From then on, if the caitiffs seek to uphold our covenant, we shall pacify them with open sincerity, neither luring them for the sake of profit nor seizing them by taking advantage of their internal disorder; if from then on the caitiffs violate our covenant, we shall exercise tactical adaptability according to what is advantageous, either closing the passes to turn them away or deploying troops to punish them. Thus peace is acceptable, and war is also acceptable; using this approach to defend Shanxi and Datong is acceptable, and using it to defend all the other defense commands is also acceptable. For the initiative will always rest with us, giving us more than enough capacity to respond to changing circumstances, regardless of whether the caitiffs are strong or weak, rebellious or submissive. This is what is meant by "cultivating internal governance and putting external defenses in order, first making oneself invincible so as to await the enemy's vulnerability." Yet there is still more to be said: in antiquity, Li Mu 李牧, the fine general of Zhao, was regularly stationed in Dai and Yanmen to guard against the Xiongnu—territory that was in fact merely one corner of present-day Shanxi and Datong. Examining that era, he was nonetheless able to outfit 1,300 picked war chariots, with a commensurate number of cavalry, 50,000 warriors worth a hundred pieces of gold, and twice that number of crossbowmen; moreover, he slaughtered cattle daily to feast his troops, and in the end he was able to devise surprise tactics, routing and slaying over 100,000 Xiongnu horsemen, extinguishing the Chanlan, defeating the Donghu, forcing the Linhu to surrender, and causing the Chanyu to flee far away and not dare approach the frontiers of Zhao for over ten years. This was for no other reason than that he was entrusted with undivided authority, so that he was able to exercise his talents to the fullest. This being so, today, giving weight to the selection of commanders with autonomous frontier authority and relaxing the restrictions of bureaucratic regulations depend solely on him who commands the generals paying heed to this!

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄後序
聖天子萬曆元祀山西歲當鄉試
〔文光〕等以監臨御史聘至典
試事錄既成〔文光〕當序諸後
竊惟人才之生關乎氣運其
培養有自其奮起有期其氣
厚者必重發其應運者必非
===
數數然也在昔唐虞之盛史
稱十六族堯未能舉舜舉之
夫以堯之神智豈有遺舉哉
業已培養之蓋遺之舉也至
讀皐陶謨知人安民亦言其
人有九德其取數至備也而
三德六德咸事事不遺又若
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄後序

聖天子萬曆元祀，山西歲當鄉試，〔文光〕等以監臨御史聘至，典試事。錄既成，〔文光〕當序諸後。竊惟人才之生，關乎氣運。其培養有自，其奮起有期；其氣厚者必重發，其應運者必非數數然也。在昔唐、虞之盛，史稱十六族堯未能舉，舜舉之。夫以堯之神智，豈有遺舉哉？業已培養之，蓋遺之舉也。至讀《皐陶謨》知人安民，亦言其人有九德，其取數至備也；而三德、六德，咸事事不遺，又若
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the first year of the Wanli reign of the Sacred Son of Heaven, the calendar fell due for the Provincial Examination in Shanxi. I, [Wenguang] 〔文光〕, and others were invited by the Supervising Censor to preside over the examination affairs. Now that the record has been completed, it falls to me, [Wenguang] 〔文光〕, to write its postface.

I humbly reflect that the emergence of men of talent is bound up with the cycle of cosmic vitality. Their cultivation has its source, and their rising up has its appointed time; those whose vital endowment is deep will surely burst forth with great weight, and those who respond to the turning of the age are certainly not encountered at every turn. In antiquity, during the flourishing age of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], the histories record that the "sixteen clans" could not yet be raised to office by Yao, and it was Shun who promoted them. Now, with Yao's divine wisdom, how could he have overlooked their promotion? Rather, having already cultivated them, he left them behind to be promoted by his successor. When one reads in the "Counsels of Gao Yao" (Gao Yao mo) of knowing men and giving peace to the people, it likewise speaks of men possessing the Nine Virtues, making the criteria for selection most comprehensive; yet men of three virtues and of six virtues were all employed in affairs without any being left out, which again seems as though…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
不專備然者蓋唐虞之世政
愉而俗恬士生其間者志在
大同必於求治旣自量己以
致力而不辭又量人知其必
能致力己無媿慚而人亦無
他讓故曰九德咸事言收之
者備也于時人皆君子比屋
可封則彼都人士遺而待舉
者多矣非舜爲收哉三晉古
唐虞夏故都也其薰蒸緼結
代產異才當
穆宗皇帝撫運中興內寧外輯環
邊無烽燧之警而絃誦之教
頓追往昔惟
punctuated: 不專備然者。蓋唐虞之世，政愉而俗恬，士生其間者，志在大同，必於求治，旣自量己以致力而不辭，又量人知其必能致力，己無媿慚，而人亦無他讓，故曰「九德咸事」，言收之者備也。于時人皆君子，比屋可封，則彼都人士遺而待舉者多矣，非舜爲收哉？三晉，古唐、虞、夏故都也，其薰蒸緼結，代產異才。當穆宗皇帝撫運中興，內寧外輯，環邊無烽燧之警，而絃誦之教頓追往昔。惟
translation_en: …as if it did not require completeness in a single individual. For in the age of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], governance was harmonious and customs were tranquil. Scholars born in that era set their aspirations on the Great Unity and were resolved upon seeking good order. Having measured themselves, they exerted their strength without declining; and having measured others, they knew that others could likewise exert their strength. They themselves felt no shame, nor did others yield out of deference. Therefore it is said, "All the nine virtues are employed in service," which means that the gathering in of talent was comprehensive. At that time, everyone was a gentleman, and every household side by side was worthy of enfeoffment. Thus, among the men of refinement in those capitals, there were many who had been left behind to await promotion—and was it not Shun who gathered them in? The Three Jin region [Shanxi] is the site of the ancient capitals of Tang, Yu, and Xia. Steeped in and bound together by this influence, it has produced extraordinary talents from generation to generation. When Emperor Muzong responded to Heaven's turn of destiny and achieved a dynastic restoration, the interior was peaceful and the exterior was brought into harmony; along the surrounding frontiers there were no alarms from beacon fires, and the teaching of stringed instruments and recitation suddenly rivaled the past.
