title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
皇上重華協帝首重選舉俯納言
官條議頒布視昔有加則培
養者既厚而應期者當輩出
唐虞諸臣類皆冀產于時有
洛命不洛之命則所稱九德
蓋已難之矣今晉之山川猶
故也假令時代稍侵下於唐
===
虞左右之臣不無遜避其於
君子可封之輩當不多讓〔文〕
〔光〕甞頓轡境上俯仰大行汾
流奇雲異蜃相出沒巳覘窺
必有異材伏處其下矣夫石
韞則山輝珠潛則川媚人才
之生類是也矧三晉爲帝王
punctuated: 皇上重華協帝，首重選舉，俯納言官條議，頒布視昔有加。則培養者既厚，而應期者當輩出。唐、虞諸臣，類皆冀產，于時有洛命、不洛之命，則所稱九德，蓋已難之矣。今晉之山川猶故也，假令時代稍侵，下於唐、虞左右之臣，不無遜避；其於君子可封之輩，當不多讓。〔文〕〔光〕甞頓轡境上，俯仰大行、汾流，奇雲異蜃相出沒，巳覘窺必有異材伏處其下矣。夫石韞則山輝，珠潛則川媚，人才之生，類是也。矧三晉爲帝王
translation_en: … His Majesty matches the ancient emperors in double-splendor; he gives foremost importance to the selection and recommendation of talent, and has deigned to accept the itemized proposals of the Speaking Officials, promulgating regulations that go even further than in the past. Thus, since the nurturing of talent has been so generous, those who answer the call of the age ought to emerge in great numbers. The various ministers of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] mostly hailed from Jizhou; yet even at that time there were some who received the charge through consultation and some who did not [? 洛命不洛之命, for 咨命不咨之命], which shows that attaining the so-called Nine Virtues was already considered difficult. Today the mountains and rivers of Jin remain just as of old. Even supposing our era has somewhat declined and cannot help yielding precedence to the flanking ministers of Tang and Yu, when it comes to the ranks of noble men whose households were all worthy of enfeoffment, our men should not fall far behind. I, [Wen][guang] 〔文〕〔光〕, once halted my horse's reins at the border, looking up and down at the Taihang Mountains and the currents of the Fen River, where wondrous clouds and strange mirages appeared and vanished by turns; from this I already glimpsed that there must be extraordinary talents lying hidden beneath them. Now, when jade is enclosed within rock, the mountain shines; when pearls lie submerged, the stream charms: the birth of human talent is just like this. How much more so given that the Three Jin were the ancient capitals of sovereigns and kings…

title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
中有稽古自樹者卽不能如
十六相而三德六德勉自循
服是皆
先帝有以遺之也第其心與言違
功與言異言者〔文光〕所據而
知人者也言不可必從而試
之功又從而鑑之此於進取
===
曷據哉嘗聞之鳳之性至仁
其文五色昭明似鳳性至不
仁其文亦五色植桃李者謂
其華實也不幸變爲荆棘則
將何利而取材爲哉〔文光〕恐
多士文似而心違與旣收而
變者或類於是唐虞試功幽
punctuated: 中有稽古自樹者，卽不能如十六相，而三德、六德勉自循服，是皆先帝有以遺之也。第其心與言違，功與言異；言者，〔文光〕所據而知人者也。言不可必，從而試之功，又從而鑑之，此於進取曷據哉？嘗聞之：鳳之性至仁，其文五色；昭明似鳳，性至不仁，其文亦五色。植桃李者，謂其華實也，不幸變爲荆棘，則將何利而取材爲哉？〔文光〕恐多士文似而心違，與旣收而變者，或類於是。唐虞試功幽
translation_en: …among them there are those who study antiquity to establish themselves; even if they cannot match the Sixteen Worthies, they strive to abide by the three virtues and the six virtues—all of this is bequeathed to them by the Late Emperor. Yet if their hearts run counter to their words, and their deeds differ from their words—words being what I, [Tan] Wenguang 〔文光〕, rely upon to judge men—if words cannot be trusted, so that one must proceed to test them by their deeds and then examine them accordingly, what basis would remain for selecting and advancing them? I have heard that the nature of the phoenix (feng) is utmost benevolence, and its plumage is of five colors; the zhaoming bird resembles the phoenix, yet its nature is utmost malevolence, while its plumage is also of five colors. Those who plant peaches and plums do so for their blossoms and fruit; if, unfortunately, they turn into thorns and brambles, what benefit can be gained in gathering material from them? I, Wenguang 〔文光〕, fear that if the many scholars have writings that resemble [virtue] while their hearts diverge from it, or if they change after having been selected, they may be something like this. title: 萬曆元年山西鄉試錄
text:
明之典於
昭代有嚴豈惟爲古昔羞而於當
時愛育掄材之意重有負矣
此〔文光〕之所以懼而惓惓爲
多士諷且規也
直隸鎮江府儒學教授譚〔文〕
〔光〕謹序
punctuated:
明之典，於昭代有嚴，豈惟爲古昔羞，而於當時愛育掄材之意，重有負矣。此〔文光〕之所以懼，而惓惓爲多士諷且規也。
直隸鎮江府儒學教授譚〔文光〕謹序。
translation_en:
…and promotion of the worthy—a statute strictly upheld in our Illustrious Dynasty—how would they merely bring shame upon antiquity? Indeed, they would gravely betray the present era's intention in lovingly nurturing and selecting talent. This is why I, [Wen-guang], am fearful and earnestly offer this admonition and counsel to the many scholars.

Respectfully prefaced by Tan [Wenguang] 譚文光, Instructor of the Prefectural Confucian School of Zhenjiang Prefecture in the Metropolitan Area.
